p: Peak Wildlife Park is a great size for a family outing, with enough to see to fill a good few hours but not so much that the kids flag halfway round. Get close to the lemurs, catch a penguin feed if it's on and keep a look out for the red pandas, who often snooze high in the branches. A packed lunch and a flask are never a bad idea up on the moors, and a picnic with that view is hard to beat.

The park sits on the A523 between Leek and Ashbourne, close to the Derbyshire border, so it's handy for a wider trip around the southern Peak District. Just north of Leek, Rudyard Lake has a narrow-gauge steam railway running along its shore, plus boat hire and lakeside paths. In Leek itself, Brindley Water Mill, linked with the canal engineer James Brindley, is a small but fascinating heritage stop. Tittesworth Reservoir has walking trails, play areas and wide views across to The Roaches, a dramatic gritstone ridge loved by walkers and climbers.

Head the other way and the Manifold Valley is beautiful walking country, with the Manifold Way following an old railway line beneath the gaping mouth of Thor's Cave. Dovedale and Ilam Park, a National Trust estate, are famous for their stepping stones and limestone scenery. Thrill-seekers will know that Alton Towers is within easy reach too, so you could plan a weekend of animals on one day and big rides on the next. All in all, this corner of Staffordshire has more going for it than many people realise.
